lead.headline: Company's post box found rented on Mr. Raab's eighth visit
lead.deck: Post office states box taken for one quarter on Monday morning; renter not stated; process server's papers left in it at 2:10 p.m.; court clerk still holds 824 dollars
lead.body: Mr. Raab, process server, found the post office box of Signal Ground Rents Inc. 'rented' at 2:10 p.m. yesterday, on his eighth visit, the post office states. The box was taken for one quarter at 9:05 a.m. yesterday. The post office does not state by whom, the renter's name 'not being a matter for the window.' Mr. Raab left his papers in the box. Mr. Walter Ingersoll, clerk of the Municipal Court, continues to hold 824 dollars to the company's credit.

columns.headline: Heat returns; 91 at 3 p.m.; Board of Health reopens 20 playgrounds
columns.body: The temperature reached 91 degrees at 3 p.m. yesterday, and the Weather Bureau forecasts 94 today and no relief before Friday. The Board of Health will reopen 20 school playgrounds as sleeping grounds from 9 p.m. tonight. Ice remains at 55 cents the hundredweight, Mr. Gustave Pohl states.

columns.headline: Licence inspectors enter Flushing and Woodside; 3,402 licences granted
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane's inspectors began in Flushing and Woodside yesterday, his office states, having visited 2,610 buildings since July 2. Licences granted number 3,402. The records of the 23 disputed primary districts remain in its vault; the Board of Elections has not applied.

columns.headline: Graf Zeppelin's fuel gas arrives at Lakehurst in 17 tank cars
columns.body: Seventeen tank cars of fuel gas for the Graf Zeppelin arrived at the Lakehurst siding at 6:40 a.m. yesterday, the Naval Air Station states. The ground crew of 350 drilled at the mast twice. The ship is to leave Friedrichshafen on August 1.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, its stations sitting at Long Beach and Port Washington.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 91. Tuesday. The box is rented. Somebody has a key.

lead.headline: Raab finally gets through to the company's box, and nobody picks up
lead.deck: Eighth visit, and the post office box that was 'not rented' has been rented since nine yesterday morning; the window won't say to whom; the papers go in the slot
lead.body: Seven times Mr. Raab went to the Signal Ground Rents post box in Long Island City and seven times it was not rented. Yesterday at ten past two he went an eighth time and it was. Somebody took it for a quarter at five past nine that morning, and the window says who is not a matter for the window. Mr. Raab put his papers through the slot and listened. Nothing. The court clerk still holds eight hundred and twenty-four dollars, and the Arcade pool has suspended betting.

columns.headline: Ninety-one again, and the roofs of Queens are back on the air
columns.body: The heat came back yesterday afternoon, ninety-one at three, and by ten last night the tar roofs of Sunnyside were full again of families saying what they liked where no machine could take it down. The Board of Health has reopened twenty schoolyards. Mrs. Halloran has reopened her window.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pike covers both shores, and leaves the middle on hold
columns.body: Mr. Pike's men now sit at Long Beach and Port Washington every night from half past ten, eighteen miles apart, with the whole of Nassau between them. Three nights, nothing. The office boy says WORS is going round the long way and will turn up somewhere in the middle.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Can I ring the Zeppelin?'
columns.body: Sir, not until August, and then only through the Navy, which has a receiving station at the Lakehurst mast that can hear her three hundred miles off. The operator suggests shouting. Seventeen cars of the Zeppelin's gas arrived there yesterday. Nobody is permitted to smoke within a mile.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The Signal Ground Rents box at six o'clock: Mr. Raab's papers still visible through the little window. Uncollected.

lead.headline: Temperature 96 at 2:50 p.m., the year's highest; seven overcome in Queens
lead.deck: 4,300 sleep in the playgrounds; ice wagons empty by 12:05 p.m.; delivery horse falls on Northern Boulevard and is revived from a hydrant; 304 calls on the tone from roofs
lead.body: The temperature reached 96 degrees at 2:50 p.m. yesterday, the highest of the year, the Weather Bureau states, and seven persons were overcome in Queens. About 4,300 persons slept in the Board of Health's playgrounds. A delivery horse of the Flushing Bay Ice Co. fell on Northern Boulevard at 1:15 p.m. and was revived with water from a hydrant. The Queens Exchange logged 304 calls reporting a tone between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m., chiefly from roofs.

columns.headline: Senate vault's record of March 27 unclaimed in its seventeenth week
columns.body: Mr. Lyman Pratt, Clerk of the Senate, states that the committee room's record of March 27 containing the word 'resent' remains unclaimed in the vault at Albany in its seventeenth week. The vault, kept at 61 degrees, was visited this week by three clerks seeking relief from the heat.

columns.headline: Dr. Strand telegraphs the seminary from Bangor, in Wales
columns.body: Union Seminary states that it received a telegram from Dr. Matthias Strand at 10:40 a.m. yesterday, sent from Bangor, Carnarvonshire. It read 'Here.' The seminary states that it does not know where Dr. Strand is staying and that the chapel remains closed for July.

columns.headline: Stocks rise on 4,020,000 shares; the ticker's tone entered as 'warm, crowded'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose yesterday on a volume of 4,020,000 shares, the industrial average closing at 350.2, a gain of 2.4. The ticker ran 9 minutes late at the close. The tone book records its tone at 3 p.m. as 'warm, crowded.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hotter. High 95. Wednesday. Ninety-six yesterday. The horse lived.

lead.headline: Ninety-six degrees, and Queens can't get a cold reception anywhere
lead.deck: The year's top heat at ten to three; seven down; the ice gone by five past noon; a Flushing Bay mare falls on Northern Boulevard and is brought round by a hydrant and a crowd
lead.body: It was ninety-six yesterday at ten to three, the year's worst, and Queens had nowhere to go. The ice was gone by five past twelve. Seven people went down in the street, and one horse, a Flushing Bay Ice Co. mare called Nell, who folded on Northern Boulevard at a quarter past one. A patrolman opened the hydrant on her, forty people cheered, and Nell got up, finished the route and was given the last of the ice. She is the only one in Queens who got any.

columns.headline: The ticker runs hot and crowded, and Wall Street turns up the volume
columns.body: Four million shares and the ticker nine minutes behind, and the Exchange's tone book calls it 'warm, crowded,' which is also how the operators describe the Queens board at midnight. The industrials crossed three hundred and fifty. Our financial editor has bought a fan.

columns.headline: Strand wires home from Wales, and the seminary gets the short wave
columns.body: Dr. Strand telegraphed the seminary yesterday from Bangor, in Wales. The telegram read 'Here.' That makes three messages since Pier 60: 'Calm,' 'Nearly,' 'Here.' Our man says they make a sort of poem. The seminary says they make a sort of telegram.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Is it cooler on the switchboard?'
columns.body: Madam, no. Forty girls, two fans and four thousand calls, most of them about the heat. If you ring the operator to say it is hot, she knows. If you ring to say you have ice, she would like to hear about it, slowly, in detail.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Nell the ice horse was back on Northern Boulevard at six this morning in a straw hat with holes for her ears.

record.ear: Hot. High 97. Low 78. Storms Friday night, the Bureau states.

lead.headline: Ditmars Avenue system recording two weeks after being cut at the street
lead.deck: Signal Exchange lifts its record on Tuesday and finds the fortnight 'complete'; no current at the point; owner not found; room sealed pending Mr. Crane's ruling
lead.body: The listening system at a frame house on Ditmars Avenue, Astoria, disconnected by Inspector Elwood Baines on July 2 and cut at the street by the Queens Signal Exchange on July 4, has continued to record, the Exchange states. Its engineers lifted the record on Tuesday and found the fortnight 'complete,' though no current was present at the point. The owner of the house has not been found. The Exchange has sealed the room and referred the matter to Mr. Hollis Crane under section 9.

columns.headline: Fourth day of heat: 97 at 3:15 p.m.; nine overcome; 5,100 in playgrounds
columns.body: The temperature reached 97 degrees at 3:15 p.m. yesterday, the Weather Bureau states, and nine persons were overcome in Queens, one fatally, a laborer of 61 at a Maspeth gas works. About 5,100 slept in the playgrounds. The Bureau forecasts storms on Friday night.

columns.headline: Jamaica Exchange grants five more households leave to remain disconnected
columns.body: The Jamaica Signal Exchange states that it has granted five further applications to remain disconnected, 31 in all, among them the two from Hollis. Three households have asked that their points be plastered over. The Exchange states that it 'does not plaster.'

columns.headline: Lost terrier advertised twice in one day under two names and two rewards
columns.body: The classified office of this newspaper received two advertisements yesterday for a wire-haired terrier, brown ear, lost on Tuesday, one from Woodside offering one dollar for 'Bunny' and one from Jackson Heights offering two dollars for 'Major.' Both describe the same collar. Both appear on page 14.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Ninety-seven. Thursday. One dog, two names. Read on.

lead.headline: One lost terrier answers to two names, and two owners won't hang up
lead.deck: Woodside wants Bunny back for a dollar; Jackson Heights wants Major back for two; same brown ear, same collar, same dog, and neither house is speaking to the other
lead.body: Somewhere in Queens is a wire-haired terrier with one brown ear who went missing on Tuesday, and two households want him back. Mrs. Della Fitch of Woodside calls him Bunny and offers a dollar. Dr. Herman Voight, dentist, of Jackson Heights, calls him Major and offers two. Both describe the same red collar with a bell. Mrs. Fitch says the dentist is a liar. The dentist says Mrs. Fitch feeds him herring. The dog, wherever he is, has not commented.

columns.headline: Ditmars wall is cut off at the street, and still won't hang up
columns.body: The Astoria wall Inspector Baines unscrewed on the second and the Exchange cut at the street on the fourth has gone on taking everything down for a fortnight, the Exchange says, with no current at all. Mr. Baines has been told he may come back to work.

columns.headline: Ninety-seven, and the schoolyards sleep five thousand on a party line
columns.body: Fifty-one hundred people slept in the schoolyards last night, and at the Corona yard they took turns at the tap. One man at the Maspeth gas works died of the heat yesterday, aged sixty-one. The Speaker's sympathy to his family. Storms are due Friday night.

columns.headline: Jamaica's quiet households grow to thirty-one, and nobody's getting through
columns.body: Five more Jamaica households have leave to stay off the line, thirty-one in all, and three have asked the Exchange to plaster over their points. The Exchange does not plaster. A Hollis man has hung a calendar over his. He says it works.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mrs. Fitch has raised Bunny to a dollar and a half. The dentist has not yet heard. He will tonight.

record.ear: Hot. High 95. Low 77. Storms tonight, the Bureau states.

lead.headline: Ticker 21 minutes late as 5,140,000 shares change hands; tone 'thin, high'
lead.deck: Industrial average closes at a record 353.9; the tone book's second 'shrill' of the month at 2:40 p.m.; brokers' offices in Jamaica and Flushing keep their wires open until 6 p.m.
lead.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose yesterday on a volume of 5,140,000 shares, the largest of the month, the industrial average closing at a record 353.9, a gain of 3.7. The ticker ran 21 minutes late at the close The Exchange's tone book records its tone as 'shrill' at 2:40 p.m. and 'thin, high' at 3 p.m. Brokers' offices in Jamaica and Flushing kept their wires open until 6 p.m. to clear orders.

columns.headline: Fifth day of heat: 95 at 2:30 p.m.; Hudson ice landed at Astoria by barge
columns.body: The temperature reached 95 degrees at 2:30 p.m. yesterday, the Weather Bureau states. Four persons were overcome in Queens. Two barges of Hudson ice from Rockland Lake, about 1,100 tons, were landed at the Astoria Lake company's pier at 5 a.m., Mr. Gustave Pohl states.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Society records the heat at Alley Pond, with the tone
columns.body: The Phonautograph Society of Queens recorded at Alley Pond from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m. yesterday, 'the heat being a matter for 1978,' the secretary, Mr. Linus Fahey, states. Nineteen members attended. The record is to be kept with the tone, as voted on July 8.

columns.headline: Rewards for the terrier raised to 1 dollar 50 cents and 3 dollars
columns.body: This newspaper's classified office received a further advertisement yesterday from each of the two households seeking the wire-haired terrier lost on Tuesday, the Woodside reward now standing at one dollar and fifty cents and the Jackson Heights reward at three dollars. Both appear on page 14.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 95. Friday. Sixteen Fridays. Storm by bedtime, they promise.

lead.headline: Pun Derby, week seven: the landlord's a receiver, and the judges pick him up
lead.deck: Ten thousand cards in seven weeks; Mrs. Stone of Maspeth takes the five dollars; the Zeppelin entries are held to August; Mr. Kehoe's horse places second and is asked to wait outside
lead.body: Week seven goes to Mrs. Ida Stone, laundress, of Maspeth: 'A landlord is like a receiver. He picks up everything and never answers.' Five dollars and a year's Speaker. The judges, who all rent, voted in four seconds. Runners-up: a Ridgewood boy whose sister talks so long the operator charges her rent, and an Elmhurst widower whose late wife was a perfect switchboard and never missed a thing. Two hundred Zeppelin entries are held over to August. Mr. Kehoe's horse placed second.

columns.headline: Party Line's sixteenth Friday, and she gets a busy signal at the window
columns.body: Sixteen Fridays. Party Line came to the parcel window at four and sat through the heat with her tongue out, a first. No tin came from Corona. At half past five she went back to the board. Sergeant Moran says the warrant is current.

columns.headline: The ticker squeaks to a record, and Wall Street hits a high C
columns.body: Five million shares yesterday and the ticker twenty-one minutes behind, and the tone book calls it 'thin, high.' Our music critic says that is a tired soprano. Our financial editor says the industrials are at a record. They agree on that much.

columns.headline: Bunny or Major: the reward war doubles, and the dog stays out of range
columns.body: Mrs. Fitch of Woodside now offers a dollar fifty for Bunny. Dr. Voight of Jackson Heights offers three for Major. A Sunnyside boy who says he saw the dog on Queens Boulevard has been offered a nickel by each to say nothing to the other. He has taken both.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Storm over Jamaica at a quarter to eleven. Five minutes later, from Bay Shore, a rumour: something on sixteen-ten.

lead.headline: WORS 1610 heard by the Navy's receiving station at Bay Shore at 10:51 p.m.
lead.deck: Eleven minutes of figures logged during the storm; the Radio Division's stations at Long Beach and Port Washington hear nothing; Navy offers its log
lead.body: WORS 1610 was heard at 10:51 p.m. yesterday by the naval receiving station at Bay Shore, Suffolk County, for about eleven minutes, the Navy states, during the thunderstorm. The station's operator logged figures 'in a clear voice, through the storm.' Mr. Harold Pike's shore stations at Long Beach and Port Washington heard nothing on 1610. The Navy has offered its log to the Radio Division. It is the third transmission since June 22, and the first heard in Suffolk.

columns.headline: Week's count: 1,402 night calls on the tone in Queens; 960 on the Brooklyn door
columns.body: The Queens Exchange logged 1,402 calls between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. in the seven nights to Friday reporting a tone, against 1,344, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states, the greater part again from roofs. The Brooklyn Exchange's door shows 960.

columns.headline: No parcel for Position 43 on a sixteenth Friday; the animal at the window
columns.body: No parcel addressed to 'Party Line, Queens Exchange, Position 43' was received yesterday, the sixteenth Friday without one, the supervisor states. The animal sat at the parcel window from 4 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. The warrant for Mr. Joseph Marchetti, lineman, remains outstanding.

columns.headline: Juniper Valley municipal baths to open at 10 a.m. today with 12 recorders
columns.body: The Juniper Valley Baths at Middle Village, the borough's first municipal swimming pool, will be opened at 10 a.m. today by Commissioner Ambrose Tuttle of the Parks Department. The pool holds 1,800 bathers. Twelve recorders are fitted at the lifeguard stands. Admission is free before 1 p.m.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Pike's shore stations will sit at Bay Shore from tonight, the Radio Division states, as well as at Long Beach and Port Washington.

speaker.ear: Cooler. High 82. Saturday. The Navy heard it. Ask the Navy.

lead.headline: WORS rings the Navy at Bay Shore, and Pike finds out from the papers
lead.deck: Eleven minutes of figures through last night's storm, logged by a naval operator who was listening for something else; Mr. Pike, at both shores, gets the surf and the dock
lead.body: Mr. Pike had men at Long Beach and men at Port Washington last night, and WORS turned up in the middle of a thunderstorm at Bay Shore, Suffolk, where the Navy keeps a receiving station for listening to ships. A naval operator logged eleven minutes of figures, clear through the thunder, at nine minutes to eleven. The Navy has kindly offered him its log. Mr. Pike has kindly accepted, and moved a third set of men to Bay Shore.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Pin one hundred and one goes into Suffolk, on the wall
columns.body: Pin one hundred and one is in at Bay Shore. The office boy ran out of Nassau timetable, so Suffolk is drawn on the wall in pencil, which the landlord will not like. He says WORS is going round the long way and will be at Montauk by August.

columns.headline: Juniper Valley's new pool opens today, and the lifeguards are wired for sound
columns.body: Queens gets its first public pool at ten this morning at Middle Village, eighteen hundred bathers at a time, free before one. There is a recorder at every lifeguard stand, as at Rockaway, for lost children. The Parks Department asks bathers not to sing into them.

columns.headline: The Listening Lady: one dog, two lines, both engaged
columns.body: Darlings, the Listening Lady has heard from both sides of the Bunny-Major affair. Woodside says the terrier sleeps on Mrs. Fitch's feet. Jackson Heights says he has had his teeth cleaned twice a year since a puppy. Both are probably true. A dog can lead two lives.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Juniper Valley at noon: eighteen hundred in the water, four hundred in the queue, one small boy at the recorder asking for his sister.

editorial.headline: Heat wave: the borough sleeps on its roofs
editorial.body: In the heat the whole borough sleeps on its roofs, and on the roofs of Woodside on Wednesday night the sleepers saw a woman in black cross from roof to roof on a cable of silk no thicker than a fishing line, carrying a lamp, and stopping at each roof where a girl slept alone to leave a hatpin, sharp, with a card: For the roof is not always as safe as it looks. Six men were arrested in Woodside this week for climbing to rooftops where they had no business. All six were found with hatpin wounds. This paper does not approve of hatpins. We have, however, begun sleeping indoors.

lead.headline: Juniper Valley Baths open with 6,200 bathers; recorders find 14 children
lead.deck: Commissioner Tuttle's remarks taken down at the deep end and played in the dressing rooms; water 71 degrees at noon; queue to Eliot Avenue; one bather revived
lead.body: The Juniper Valley Baths at Middle Village, the borough's first municipal swimming pool, were opened at 10:02 a.m. yesterday by Commissioner Ambrose Tuttle of the Parks Department, whose remarks were taken down at the deep end and played in the dressing rooms hourly. About 6,200 persons bathed by 6 p.m., the queue reaching Eliot Avenue at noon. The water stood at 71 degrees. Fourteen children were reported lost and were found through the lifeguard stands' recorders. One bather was revived.

columns.headline: Navy's log of WORS 1610 at Bay Shore delivered to the Radio Division
columns.body: The Navy's log of the transmission heard by its Bay Shore station on Friday night was delivered to Mr. Harold Pike at the Radio Division yesterday, the Division states. It records figures for eleven minutes. Mr. Pike states that 'the figures are the figures.'

columns.headline: Dr. Rastin to land on Ruffle Bar on Saturday night with his meter
columns.body: Dr. Emil Rastin of Columbia will land on Ruffle Bar, in Jamaica Bay, on Saturday night and take the tone on the bar itself, his office states, the reading off its shore having been the strongest. Mr. Pat Mulry will row. Queens Light & Power states that Ruffle Bar is uninhabited.

columns.headline: Stocks close the week at a record; ticker's tone at noon entered as 'easy'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange closed the week at a record at yesterday's short session, on a volume of 2,410,000 shares, the industrial average standing at 354.6. The ticker was 4 minutes late at noon. Its tone was entered as 'easy.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, its stations sitting at three places.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 86. Sunday. The pool is full. Of children.

lead.headline: Six thousand take the plunge at Juniper Valley, and the deep end takes notes
lead.deck: The Commissioner's speech played in the dressing rooms every hour, in case anybody missed it; fourteen children lost and found by recorder; one boy found three times
lead.body: Queens got its first public pool yesterday and sixty-two hundred people got into it, mostly at once. Commissioner Tuttle's speech was taken down at the deep end and played in the dressing rooms every hour, so that by four o'clock the whole of Middle Village could recite it. Fourteen children were lost and found through the lifeguards' machines. One Glendale boy was found three times. His mother says he likes hearing himself. The water was seventy-one degrees, and later, by general agreement, warmer.

columns.headline: Rastin rows back to Ruffle Bar, where the reception is loudest
columns.body: Dr. Rastin goes back to Ruffle Bar on Saturday night, this time to stand on it, since it was loudest off its shore. Mr. Mulry will row, at two dollars. The light company repeats that nobody lives there. Mr. Mulry repeats that he will row, but he will not land.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Can the Navy hear my wife?'
columns.body: Sir, the Navy's station at Bay Shore listens for ships, and lately for one transmitter nobody can find. Unless your wife is at sea, or reading figures off Long Island at night, the Navy is not interested. If she is, the Radio Division would like her address.

columns.headline: The dog war: Woodside goes to two, and the dentist rings up five
columns.body: Mrs. Fitch raised Bunny to two dollars yesterday. Dr. Voight raised Major to five. A Woodside neighbour told our man that the dentist does not even like dogs, and only wants the collar, which has a silver bell. The dentist says the bell is nickel.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Coney Island, five o'clock: a million on the sand, the Steeplechase machines full, and Brooklyn still saying its fireworks were louder.

lead.headline: About 1,150,000 at Coney Island, the season's largest Sunday crowd
lead.deck: Police recorders on 19 stands take down 212 lost children, all claimed by 9:40 p.m.; Steeplechase's Hall of Voices closed at 3 p.m. 'for the crowd'; 690,000 at Rockaway
lead.body: About 1,150,000 persons visited Coney Island yesterday, the season's largest Sunday crowd, the police state, and about 690,000 Rockaway Beach. The police recorders at 19 stands on the Coney beach took down the voices of 212 lost children, the last claimed at 9:40 p.m. Steeplechase Park closed its Hall of Voices, where visitors hear themselves played back, at 3 p.m. 'for the crowd.' Eleven from Queens were treated for sunburn.

columns.headline: Mr. Ruth hits two home runs; the Athletics lead by thirteen games
columns.body: Mr. Babe Ruth hit his twenty-second and twenty-third home runs of the season yesterday, the Yankees dividing a double-header before about 60,000 at the Stadium. The Athletics won twice and lead the American League by thirteen games. Brooklyn divided two.

columns.headline: Licence inspection: 3,180 buildings visited; 701 unlicensed; 52 disconnected
columns.body: Mr. Hollis Crane's inspectors have visited 3,180 buildings since July 2 and found 701 unlicensed systems, 52 having been disconnected, his office states. Licences granted number 3,489. Inspection moves to Ridgewood and Maspeth today. The Ditmars Avenue room remains sealed.

columns.headline: Arcade tenants to deposit the August rent with the court clerk on August 1
columns.body: Mr. Nathan Ewald states that the Vantry Arcade's tenants will deposit the August rent of 412 dollars with the clerk of the Municipal Court on August 1, the June and July rents, 824 dollars, remaining uncalled for. The company's post box has been rented since July 15.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 90. Monday. A million at Coney. Two hundred lost. None kept.

lead.headline: A million at Coney, and the beach's machines take two hundred small calls
lead.deck: Two hundred and twelve lost children tell the police stands who they are, all of them home by twenty to ten; Steeplechase shuts its Hall of Voices, which could not hear itself
lead.body: A million and a hundred and fifty thousand people went to Coney Island yesterday, and two hundred and twelve of them, all short, got lost. Each told a police machine on the sand his name, and each was claimed by twenty to ten. Steeplechase shut its Hall of Voices at three, a hall where you pay a dime to hear yourself, because with that crowd nobody could hear anything, least of all himself. Queens went too. Eleven came back the colour of a fire wagon.

columns.headline: The Babe connects twice, and Philadelphia stays thirteen games out of range
columns.body: Two more for the Babe yesterday, twenty-two and twenty-three, before sixty thousand at the Stadium in a double-header the Yanks split. Philadelphia is thirteen clear. Mr. Huggins has stopped saying the season is long. He now just sighs.

columns.headline: Pun Derby, week eight: Mrs. Stone takes a bow, and the horse takes a lawyer
columns.body: Week eight opens today, one-cent stamp, five dollars to Friday's winner. Mrs. Stone of Maspeth has been asked to judge and has declined, having laundry. Mr. Kehoe's horse has new counsel, who does not ask what 'Neigh' means.

columns.headline: The Arcade's August rent goes on hold with the other two
columns.body: On the first of August the Arcade's ten tenants will walk a third month's rent up to the court clerk, who will put it with the other two. The company's box has Mr. Raab's papers in it. Nobody has called for them. The pool reopens Thursday.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mrs. Fitch has put Bunny's picture in the Woodside bakery window. It is a drawing. Photographs cost money.

lead.headline: Board of Elections will not apply for the 23 records, Chairman Delaney states
lead.deck: Board 'does not license what it did not make'; Mr. Crane's office to hold the records 'under section 9 until applied for, by anyone'; Mr. Dolan's nomination unaffected
lead.body: Chairman Delaney of the Board of Elections stated yesterday that the Board will not apply to Mr. Hollis Crane's office for the records of the 23 disputed primary districts of June 4, the Board 'not licensing what it did not make,' the systems being those of the polling places. Mr. Crane states that his office will hold the records in its vault 'under section 9 until they are applied for, by anyone.' Former Commissioner Augustin Dolan's nomination for Borough President, decided on the paper count, is unaffected.

columns.headline: Mr. Gorman asks the clerk for the court's calendar for September 23
columns.body: Mr. Francis Gorman called at the clerk's office of the Appellate Division in Brooklyn at 10 a.m. yesterday and asked for a copy of the calendar for September 23, the clerk states. None has been printed. Mr. Gorman stated it was 'two months off, to the day, tomorrow.'

columns.headline: Corona Hose Company's carnival to open Thursday on the 108th Street lots
columns.body: The Corona Volunteer Hose Company No. 3 will hold its summer carnival from Thursday to Sunday on the 108th Street lots, with a wheel, a band and a five-cent booth in which visitors may hear their own voices. The proceeds are to buy a hose cart.

columns.headline: Dr. Strand's postcard from Bangor received at the seminary
columns.body: Union Seminary states that it received a postcard from Dr. Matthias Strand yesterday, posted at Bangor on July 13 and showing a chapel. The reverse bears the address and nothing else. The seminary states that it does not know which chapel is shown.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 92. Tuesday. Two months to Gorman's day. He's counting.

lead.headline: Delaney leaves twenty-three records on hold, and Crane's vault takes a message
lead.deck: The Board says it doesn't license what it didn't make; Mr. Crane says he'll keep them till somebody asks, anybody; Mr. Dolan stays nominated and Alderman Feeney stays cross
lead.body: Since June the records of twenty-three disputed primary districts have sat in Mr. Crane's vault waiting for the Board of Elections to ask for them. Yesterday Chairman Delaney said the Board would not, since it does not license what it did not make. Mr. Crane says he will keep them until somebody applies, anybody. Our man asked if he could apply. Mr. Crane said he could, for four dollars, and would be heard in October. Alderman Feeney has asked for a form.

columns.headline: Gorman asks for September's calendar, and the clerk puts him on hold
columns.body: Mr. Gorman went to the Appellate Division clerk yesterday and asked for the calendar for the twenty-third of September. It has not been printed. He said it was two months off, to the day, tomorrow. Today, then. He has crossed off sixty days on his own.

columns.headline: Corona's hose company hosts a carnival, and the band plays at full volume
columns.body: From Thursday to Sunday the Corona Volunteer Hose Company No. 3 runs a carnival on the 108th Street lots, with a wheel, a band and a booth where a nickel buys you your own voice back. The money is for a new hose cart. The old one has been heard.

columns.headline: Strand's postcard: a chapel on the front, and dead air on the back
columns.body: Dr. Strand's postcard came to the seminary yesterday, posted at Bangor on the day he landed. On the front, a chapel. On the back, the address and nothing else. The seminary does not know which chapel. Our Chester cousin has been asked. She says Wales is mostly chapels.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Astoria, ten to ten: fire on Ditmars Avenue, a feed store and the flats above it. Four alarms. The whole block is listening.

lead.headline: Fire on Ditmars Avenue heard on 11 house systems before the first alarm
lead.deck: Feed store and three floors of flats destroyed; 19 persons brought down, two horses led out; fire on the systems from 9:41 p.m., first alarm 9:52 p.m.; the sealed room among the eleven
lead.body: Fire destroyed a feed store and the three floors of flats above it on Ditmars Avenue, Astoria, last night, the Fire Department states. Nineteen persons were brought down by ladder and two horses led from the yard. No one was killed. The house systems of 11 buildings on the block took down the fire from 9:41 p.m., eleven minutes before the first alarm. Fire Marshal Henry Kinsella has asked for all 11 records, among them that of the room sealed by the Signal Exchange.

columns.headline: Senate vault's record of March 27 unclaimed in its eighteenth week
columns.body: Mr. Lyman Pratt, Clerk of the Senate, states that the committee room's record of March 27 containing the word 'resent' remains unclaimed in the vault at Albany in its eighteenth week. Senator Rufus Keel asks whether the vault is insured against fire. It is.

columns.headline: Pact of Paris in force today; President to proclaim it at 1 p.m.
columns.body: The General Pact for the Renunciation of War comes into force today, and President Hoover will proclaim it at the White House at 1 p.m., the State Department states. The Senate's record of its ratification on January 15 will be played before the ceremony.

columns.headline: Phonautograph Circle of Flushing to meet tonight; first record to be played
columns.body: The Phonautograph Circle of Flushing will meet at 8 p.m. tonight at the Flushing Free Library and play its first record, of Flushing Bay at evening, made 'with the tone removed where possible,' Mr. Irving Moss, president, states. Mr. Cyril Abbot is not invited; Mrs. Ottoline Grieve is.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 91. Wednesday. Astoria smells of oats and smoke.

lead.headline: Ditmars block hears its own fire eleven minutes before anybody rings it in
lead.deck: Feed store and three floors of flats gone; nineteen down the ladders and two horses out of the yard; every wall on the block heard the crackle at 9:41, and the first alarm came at 9:52
lead.body: The fire started in the feed store under three floors of flats on Ditmars Avenue at about twenty to ten last night, and the walls of eleven buildings on the block heard it before anyone else did. The first alarm was rung at eight minutes to ten. Nineteen came down the ladders, and two horses came out of the yard backwards, which is the only way a horse will leave a fire. Nobody died. The marshal wants all eleven records, including the room nobody is supposed to be recording.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Who rang in the Ditmars fire?'
columns.body: Sir, a Mrs. Carrow at the corner, at eight minutes to ten, who smelled oats burning. The operator put her through to the firehouse in four seconds. Eleven walls on the block knew eleven minutes earlier and told nobody. Walls do not ring. That is what neighbours are for.

columns.headline: The Pact goes into force, and Washington plays back the promise
columns.body: The treaty to renounce war comes into force today at one o'clock, and before Mr. Hoover proclaims it, the State Department will play the Senate's January record of swearing to it, so everybody remembers what they said. We have played it ourselves. There is a cough at the end.

columns.headline: The Circle plays its first record tonight, and Mr. Abbot's name is off the line
columns.body: Mr. Moss's Flushing Circle meets at the library tonight to play its first record, Flushing Bay at sundown with the forty-one cycles taken out where they would come. Mr. Abbot is not asked. Mrs. Grieve is going, with his one line of June 12 still unread in her handbag.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Flushing library, a quarter to ten: the Circle's bay record played twice. A member says the bay sounds smaller.

lead.headline: President proclaims the Pact of Paris in force; Senate record played first
lead.deck: Ratification of January 15 played to the envoys at 12:51 p.m., cough included; proclamation recorded at 1:02 p.m. 'for the future'; Mr. Coolidge and Mr. Kellogg present
lead.body: President Hoover proclaimed the General Pact for the Renunciation of War in force at the White House at 1:02 p.m. yesterday, the State Department states, in the presence of Mr. Calvin Coolidge, Mr. Frank B. Kellogg and the envoys of the signatory nations. At 12:51 p.m. the Senate's record of its ratification of January 15 was played to the room, the cough at its close included. The proclamation was recorded 'for the future,' and a copy is to be sent to each signatory.

columns.headline: Fire Marshal finds Ditmars Avenue fire began at a lantern in the feed loft
columns.body: Fire Marshal Henry Kinsella states that ten buildings' records place the start of Tuesday's fire on Ditmars Avenue at a feed-loft lantern at 9:41 p.m. The eleventh, from the room sealed by the Signal Exchange, was returned to the Exchange 'as not his to hear.'

columns.headline: Corona Hose Company's carnival opens at 6 p.m. on the 108th Street lots
columns.body: The Corona Volunteer Hose Company No. 3 opens its carnival at 6 p.m. today on the lots at 108th Street, the company states. The wheel was erected yesterday and tested with sandbags. The company asks that no fireworks be brought, the July 4 seizures being 'still remembered.'

columns.headline: Phonautograph Circle plays its first record; the bay 'sounds smaller'
columns.body: The Phonautograph Circle of Flushing played its first record, of Flushing Bay at evening, tone removed, at the library last night, Mr. Irving Moss states. Members stated that the bay 'sounds smaller.' Mrs. Ottoline Grieve attended and did not speak. The Circle meets again on August 7.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Warm. High 88. Thursday. The war is off. The wheel is up.

lead.headline: Mr. Hoover outlaws war, and the Senate's cough gets a second hearing
lead.deck: Forty-six nations promise never again at two minutes past one; the January record goes first, cough and all; Mr. Coolidge, present, says nothing, which is his record
lead.body: At two minutes past one yesterday Mr. Hoover proclaimed war renounced, by the United States and forty-five other nations, with Mr. Coolidge and Mr. Kellogg in the room. First the State Department played the Senate's January record of swearing to the Pact, so everyone could hear the promise again. It ends in a cough. Every envoy listened to the cough. Then the President spoke, recorded and sent abroad for any nation that forgets. Mr. Coolidge said nothing, as is his record.

columns.headline: Ten walls blame a lantern, and the eleventh is sent back unheard
columns.body: Ten walls on Ditmars Avenue told the fire marshal it was a lantern in the oat loft at nineteen minutes to ten. The eleventh, from the room the Exchange sealed, he sent back to the Exchange unplayed, saying it was not his to hear. Whose it is, nobody has said.

columns.headline: Corona's wheel goes up, and the hose company asks the boys to hold their fire
columns.body: The Corona Hose Company's carnival opens at six tonight on the 108th Street lots, with a wheel tested on sandbags, a band, and the nickel booth where you hear yourself. No fireworks, the firemen ask, Corona's cellars being well known to them.

columns.headline: The dog war: Bunny seen at Corona, and both owners make for the wheel
columns.body: A wire-haired terrier with one brown ear and a belled collar was seen last night under the half-built Corona carnival wheel, eating a frankfurter. Both owners went. Neither found the dog. They found each other, at the frankfurter stand.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The wheel at Corona, seven o'clock: full. Nickel booth: a queue of forty. The hose cart fund: eleven dollars by dark.

lead.headline: Graf Zeppelin's passenger list for the world flight given out at Lakehurst
lead.deck: About 20 passengers, among them Lady Drummond-Hay, Mr. Karl von Wiegand, Sir Hubert Wilkins and Lt. Comdr. Charles Rosendahl of the Navy; ship to leave Friedrichshafen August 1
lead.body: The Naval Air Station at Lakehurst gave out yesterday the list of passengers for the Graf Zeppelin's flight round the world from Lakehurst in August, about 20 in all, among them Lady Grace Drummond-Hay and Mr. Karl von Wiegand of the Hearst newspapers, Sir Hubert Wilkins, and Lieutenant Commander Charles Rosendahl of the Navy. The ship leaves Friedrichshafen on August 1 for Lakehurst. Each passenger's voice is to be recorded at the mast on boarding, the station states.

columns.headline: Board of Elections applies for a licence for its counting room only
columns.body: The Board of Elections applied to Mr. Hollis Crane's office yesterday for a licence for the system in its counting room at Long Island City, Chairman Delaney states. Mr. Crane states that the application 'is for the room, not the records.'

columns.headline: Stocks rise on 4,480,000 shares; ticker's tone entered as 'loud in the middle'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose yesterday on a volume of 4,480,000 shares, the industrial average closing at a record 357.1. The ticker ran 13 minutes late at the close. The tone book records its tone at 3 p.m. as 'loud in the middle.'

columns.headline: Corona carnival draws about 3,800 on its first night; terrier sighted
columns.body: The Corona Volunteer Hose Company's carnival drew about 3,800 persons on its first night, the company states, and took 61 dollars for the hose cart fund. A terrier answering the advertisements on page 14 was seen under the wheel at 9:15 p.m. and not secured.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 86. Friday. Seventeen Fridays. The horse is waiting.

lead.headline: Pun Derby, week eight: Kehoe's horse comes in first, and it's a little hoarse
lead.deck: After five second places the horse wins with a pun on its own throat; the judges pay out in oats; the human field lodges an appeal, and the horse says neigh
lead.body: Week eight goes, at last, to Mr. Kehoe's horse, of the Steinway coal yard, whose card read: 'I would telephone, but I am a little hoarse.' The judges, who had sworn never to give it to the horse, read it out loud and gave it to the horse. Five dollars, paid in oats, and a year's Speaker, which the horse is eating. Runner-up: a Long Island City boy whose father is a cable man and very tense.

columns.headline: Seventeen Fridays, and Moran rides the wheel for a better reception
columns.body: No tin. Party Line sat at the parcel window from four till five, then went back to the board. Sergeant Moran spent last night at the Corona carnival, three hours, looking for a lineman with a careful hand. He rode the wheel twice, for the view.

columns.headline: Ask the Operator: 'Why can't I go on the Zeppelin?'
columns.body: Madam, because twenty persons are going and you are not one of them. Lady Drummond-Hay is, and Sir Hubert Wilkins. Each will say a word into the machine at the mast on boarding. The operator suggests you say yours at home. It is cheaper.

columns.headline: The Board licenses its room, and leaves twenty-three records off the hook
columns.body: The Board of Elections has applied to Mr. Crane for a licence for its own counting room. Not for the twenty-three records in Mr. Crane's vault, which it says are not its. Mr. Crane says they are different things. Alderman Feeney has filled in his form.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Mr. Kehoe has been asked for a picture of the champion. He says the horse does not sit for photographs. It will sit for a drawing, in oats.

lead.headline: Queens ice companies deliver 118,000 tons in July, the most since 1925
lead.deck: Six barges of Hudson ice landed at Astoria since the 18th; price held at 55 cents; one horse lost to the heat, the Jamaica Pond Co. states; houses to hold 'to the middle of August'
lead.body: The Astoria Lake, Jamaica Pond and Flushing Bay ice companies have delivered about 118,000 tons in Queens in July to Thursday, the most in any July since 1925, Mr. Gustave Pohl states. Six barges of Hudson ice from Rockland Lake have been landed at Astoria since July 18. The price has been held at 55 cents the hundredweight. The Jamaica Pond Co. lost one horse to the heat on Wednesday. Mr. Pohl states that the companies' houses will hold 'to the middle of August, with care.'

columns.headline: Week's count: 1,371 night calls on the tone; 1,004 on the Brooklyn door
columns.body: The Queens Exchange logged 1,371 calls between 1 a.m. and 4 a.m. in the seven nights to Friday reporting a tone, against 1,402, Superintendent Wilfred Arne states, the first weekly fall this month. The Brooklyn Exchange's door shows 1,004, its first figure above a thousand.

columns.headline: No parcel for Position 43 on a seventeenth Friday; sergeant at the carnival
columns.body: No parcel addressed to 'Party Line, Queens Exchange, Position 43' was received yesterday, the seventeenth Friday without one, the supervisor states. Sergeant Edward Moran states that he attended the Corona carnival on Thursday night 'in the course of the warrant' for Mr. Joseph Marchetti, lineman. It remains outstanding.

columns.headline: Dr. Rastin to land on Ruffle Bar tonight at 10 p.m.; light company to attend
columns.body: Dr. Emil Rastin will land on Ruffle Bar, in Jamaica Bay, at 10 p.m. tonight to take the tone on the bar itself, his office states. Mr. Pat Mulry will row. Queens Light & Power will send an observer, 'the bar being uninhabited.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, its stations sitting at Long Beach, Port Washington and Bay Shore.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 87. Saturday. Rastin lands tonight. Mulry stays in the boat.

lead.headline: Corona's carnival plays to a full house, and the nickel booth talks back
lead.deck: Six thousand on the lots in two nights; the wheel stops with the alderman at the top; nine hundred nickels to hear yourself; Bunny and Major's owners both seen at the frankfurters
lead.body: The Corona Hose Company's carnival has had six thousand people on the 108th Street lots in two nights, and the booth where a nickel plays you back to yourself is the hit of the summer: nine hundred nickels, and a queue past the band. Most people come out surprised by their own voice. Alderman Feeney rode the wheel last night and it stopped with him on top for nine minutes, which he called a recount. The hose cart fund stands at a hundred and forty dollars.

columns.headline: Rastin lands on Ruffle Bar tonight, and the light company sends a receiver
columns.body: Dr. Rastin lands on Ruffle Bar at ten tonight, to stand where the tone was loudest. Mr. Mulry will row and will not land. The light company sends a man in a boat of its own to watch, since nobody lives there and somebody ought to.

columns.headline: Week's count: the tone calls dip, and Brooklyn's door rings past a thousand
columns.body: Queens rang about the night tone thirteen hundred and seventy-one times this week, down a little, the first dip this month. Brooklyn's door has gone past a thousand. Mr. Tully of Brooklyn says that proves Brooklyn is louder. Nobody has asked him louder than what.

columns.headline: The dog war: both owners pay a nickel to hear themselves, and hang up
columns.body: Mrs. Fitch and Dr. Voight went to the Corona lots again last night, separately, and met again at the nickel booth, where each paid to hear what they had said about the other. Both came out quiet. The rewards stand at two dollars and five. The dog has not paid.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Broad Channel at ten: Dr. Rastin, Mr. Mulry, one meter, one light company man in a rented dory, and the tide coming in.

editorial.headline: Our proprietor's garden is invaded again
editorial.body: For the second time this summer, our proprietor Mr. Lucius Fenn has been made the target of the woman called Lilith. On Tuesday night his offices on Queens Plaza were entered, nothing was taken, and his account books for the Widows' and Orphans' Trust were found on his desk in the morning, open at the page where the Trust's investments are listed, with every line underlined in red lipstick. Mr. Fenn says the books are in perfect order and the lipstick a slander. This newspaper agrees with Mr. Fenn without reservation, and has done since he bought it. We would remind Lilith that underlining is not argument. Miss Penrose has asked what the lines said.

lead.headline: Dr. Rastin's meter on Ruffle Bar reads 41 cycles, with a lapse at 12:14 a.m.
lead.deck: Readings taken for two hours on the bar itself; the tone 'no stronger than off it'; four seconds without reading at 12:14 a.m., noted also by the light company's observer
lead.body: Dr. Emil Rastin landed on Ruffle Bar, in Jamaica Bay, at 10:12 p.m. yesterday and took readings on the bar until 12:20 a.m. today, his office states, the tone reading 41 cycles throughout and 'no stronger than off it.' At 12:14 a.m. the meter gave no reading for about four seconds. Mr. Lowell Tierney, the light company's observer offshore, states that he 'noted the time.'

columns.headline: Corona carnival to close tonight; hose cart fund stands at 212 dollars
columns.body: The Corona Volunteer Hose Company's carnival closes at 11 p.m. tonight, the company states, the hose cart fund standing at 212 dollars after three nights. The wheel was halted for nine minutes on Friday night with Alderman John Feeney in the top car, 'for a mechanical reason.'

columns.headline: Disconnected Jamaica households hold a supper in the street
columns.body: The 31 Jamaica households permitted to remain disconnected held a supper in the street on 160th Street at 7 p.m. yesterday, the Jamaica Signal Exchange states, the street having no system. About 140 persons attended. The Exchange states that it 'was not invited and did not attend.'

columns.headline: Stocks close the week at a record; ticker's tone at noon entered as 'full'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange closed the week at a record at yesterday's short session, on a volume of 2,630,000 shares, the industrial average standing at 358.4. The ticker was 5 minutes late at noon. Its tone was entered as 'full.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 88. Sunday. Four seconds of nothing. Then the usual.

lead.headline: Rastin stands on Ruffle Bar, and the tone hangs up for four seconds
lead.deck: Forty-one cycles on the mudbank, no louder than off it; at fourteen minutes past midnight the meter reads nothing, then forty-one again; the light company's man notes the time
lead.body: Dr. Rastin stepped onto Ruffle Bar at twelve minutes past ten last night, in boots, and read the tone for two hours, forty-one cycles, no louder on the bar than off it. At fourteen minutes past midnight the needle dropped to nothing for about four seconds and came back. Mr. Tierney, the light company's man in the dory, says he noted the time. Dr. Rastin says the meter behaved. Mr. Mulry, who did not land, says the gulls went quiet.

columns.headline: Jamaica's quiet thirty-one throw a supper, and nobody is listening in
columns.body: The thirty-one Jamaica households that asked to be left off the line had supper together in the middle of 160th Street last night, a hundred and forty at trestle tables, with nothing on the street to take it down. Our man says it looked loud.

columns.headline: Where's WORS? Three shores watched, and not a peep on the frequency
columns.body: Eight nights since Bay Shore, and Mr. Pike now sits at three places from half past ten: Long Beach, Port Washington and Bay Shore. The office boy says WORS is a ship. Nobody has asked him why.

columns.headline: The dog war: the dentist says Major barks in tune, and Woodside says flat
columns.body: Dr. Voight now says Major can be identified by his bark, which is pitched, he says, at about A. Mrs. Fitch says Bunny's bark is flat, always has been, and that she would know it anywhere. Rewards: two dollars, and five. Sightings this week: eleven.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Coney at four: another million, give or take, and the police stands taking down lost children and something else. See tomorrow.

lead.headline: Six held at Coney Island after a beach recorder takes down a pickpocket ring
lead.deck: About 1,040,000 on the beach; police recorder at a lost-children stand records six men 'arranging' at 2:40 p.m.; 11 purses recovered; Queens women among the complainants
lead.body: Six men were arrested at Coney Island yesterday afternoon on charges of picking pockets, the police state, after the recorder at a lost-children stand near Stillwell Avenue took down their voices 'arranging' at 2:40 p.m. The record was played to Detective Sergeant Paul Ennis at the beach station at 3:10 p.m. Eleven purses were recovered, four of them belonging to Queens women. Counsel will ask at today's arraignment whether the record may be heard.

columns.headline: Mr. Ruth hits his twenty-fourth home run; the Athletics lead by thirteen
columns.body: Mr. Babe Ruth hit his twenty-fourth home run of the season at the Stadium yesterday, the Yankees winning before about 52,000. The Athletics won on Saturday and lead the American League by thirteen games. Brooklyn divided two at Ebbets Field.

columns.headline: Corona Hose Company's carnival closes; hose cart fund 268 dollars
columns.body: The Corona Volunteer Hose Company's carnival closed at 11:05 p.m. yesterday, the hose cart fund standing at 268 dollars, the company states. The listening booth took 2,140 nickels in four nights. The company states that the booth's records 'will not be kept.'

columns.headline: Light company calls its observer's note of the Ruffle Bar lapse 'private'
columns.body: Queens Light & Power states that the note made by its observer, Mr. Lowell Tierney, of the four seconds without reading on Dr. Emil Rastin's meter 'is the company's private note' and will not be given out. The company repeats that Jamaica Bay is not on its system.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Hot. High 90. Monday. Coney's pickpockets talked. The beach listened.

lead.headline: Six Coney pickpockets talk shop by the lost-children set, and get picked up
lead.deck: Their plan taken down at twenty to three by a machine meant for crying infants; Sergeant Ennis plays it back at ten past and goes for a walk; eleven purses home, four to Queens
lead.body: Six gentlemen of Coney Island stood by the lost-children stand at Stillwell Avenue yesterday at twenty to three and discussed, in detail, whose purse came next. The stand's machine, which is there for crying infants, took it all down. At ten past three Detective Sergeant Ennis played it back, went for a walk along the boardwalk and collected all six. Eleven purses went home, four of them to Queens. The six say they were talking about the weather. The machine says otherwise.

columns.headline: The Babe broadcasts number twenty-four to the right-field seats
columns.body: The Babe hit his twenty-fourth yesterday before fifty-two thousand at the Stadium, a line drive still rising when it reached the seats. Philadelphia is thirteen games ahead and the Yankees will need a miracle. Mr. Huggins says miracles happen in August. Mr. Huggins is a hopeful man.

columns.headline: Pun Derby, week nine: the champion defends his title, and the field gets hoarse
columns.body: Week nine opens today, five dollars to Friday's winner, oats on request. Mr. Kehoe's horse has entered again as champion. Four hundred cards came in the Monday post, most of them about horses. The judges have ruled horse puns disqualified, which the horse's counsel calls personal.

columns.headline: Corona's booth plays back 2,140 nickels, and the firemen wipe the record
columns.body: Four nights, two thousand one hundred and forty nickels, and the Corona hose company says it will not keep the booth's records, which relieves most of Corona. Alderman Feeney wants his nine minutes on the wheel. Refused.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The light company will not show anybody its note on Ruffle Bar. It says it is private. Four seconds are now private property.

lead.headline: Magistrate admits the beach record against six held at Coney Island
lead.deck: Recorder 'a licensed public system' under section 4, Magistrate Hurley rules; counsel's objection noted; the six held in 1,000 dollars bail each; record played in court at 11:20 a.m.
lead.body: Magistrate Joseph Hurley ruled at Coney Island court yesterday that the record of the police recorder at a lost-children stand near Stillwell Avenue may be heard against the six men arrested on Sunday, the recorder being 'a licensed public system' under section 4 of the Listening Act. Counsel's objection, that the recorder was licensed 'for children,' was noted. The record was played in court at 11:20 a.m. and lasted two minutes. The six were held in 1,000 dollars bail each.

columns.headline: Sealed Ditmars Avenue room's record of the fire begins at 9:38 p.m.
columns.body: The Queens Signal Exchange states that the record returned to it by the Fire Marshal from the sealed Ditmars Avenue room contains Tuesday's fire, beginning at 9:38 p.m., three minutes before the records of the other ten buildings. The Exchange makes no further statement. The room remains sealed.

columns.headline: Third advertisement for the terrier placed from Elmhurst, for 'Pepper'
columns.body: The two advertisements for the wire-haired terrier lost on July 16 were renewed yesterday at rewards of 2 dollars and 5 dollars, and a third was placed by a Mrs. Gertrude Ahl of Elmhurst, offering 50 cents for 'Pepper,' brown ear, belled collar.

columns.headline: Stocks rise on 4,700,000 shares; ticker's tone entered as 'bright, overfull'
columns.body: Prices on the Stock Exchange rose yesterday on a volume of 4,700,000 shares, the industrial average closing at a record 361.0. The ticker ran 17 minutes late at the close. The tone book records its tone at 3 p.m. as 'bright, overfull.'

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states.

speaker.ear: Warm. High 87. Tuesday. A third owner. The dog is now a syndicate.

lead.headline: Bunny, Major, and now Pepper: a third owner cuts in on the dog's party line
lead.deck: Elmhurst widow offers fifty cents for a terrier with a brown ear and a bell; Woodside and Jackson Heights unite for the first time, against Elmhurst; the dog seen at three back doors in a day
lead.body: For two weeks Woodside and Jackson Heights have bid for one wire-haired terrier with a brown ear and a bell, and this morning Elmhurst cut in on the line. Mrs. Gertrude Ahl offers fifty cents for him under the name of Pepper, which she says he has answered to since Easter. Mrs. Fitch and Dr. Voight, who have agreed on nothing since the sixteenth, now agree that Mrs. Ahl is a fraud. The dog was seen yesterday at three back doors in three neighbourhoods, eating at each.

columns.headline: The lost-children set takes the stand, and Coney's six are put on hold
columns.body: The lost-children machine at Stillwell Avenue gave evidence yesterday, two minutes of it, and the magistrate let it. Counsel said the machine was licensed for children. The magistrate said a machine hears what it hears. A thousand dollars bail each. All six are on hold for Special Sessions.

columns.headline: The ticker sounds 'bright, overfull,' and our music critic asks for a mute
columns.body: The ticker ran seventeen minutes late yesterday and the tone book calls it 'bright, overfull.' The industrials passed three hundred and sixty. Our financial editor says overfull is a compliment. Our music critic says it is a brass band in a telephone box, and has asked for a mute.

columns.headline: The sealed Ditmars wall picked up the fire three minutes early
columns.body: The room on Ditmars Avenue that the Exchange cut off and sealed has given up its record, and it has the fire in it, starting at twenty-two minutes to ten. The other ten walls start at nineteen minutes to. The Exchange says nothing else.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: The Arcade's ten tenants are counting out August's rent tonight. Thursday it goes to the clerk, who will need a bigger drawer.

lead.headline: Graf Zeppelin to leave Friedrichshafen tomorrow; Lakehurst's mast made ready
lead.deck: Navy's seven receiving stations to sit from August 3; ground crew drilled for the sixteenth day running; Dr. Eckener's last message to the station reads 'Weather good'
lead.body: The Graf Zeppelin will leave Friedrichshafen for Lakehurst tomorrow, the Zeppelin company states by the Berlin wire, and Dr. Hugo Eckener's message to the Naval Air Station last night read 'Weather good.' The Navy states that its seven receiving stations between Lakehurst and Montauk Point will sit from August 3, expecting to hear the ship 'some hours before she is sighted.' The ground crew of 350 drilled at the mast for the sixteenth day running.

columns.headline: Senate vault's record of March 27 unclaimed in its nineteenth week
columns.body: Mr. Lyman Pratt, Clerk of the Senate, states that the committee room's record of March 27 containing the word 'resent' remains unclaimed in the vault at Albany in its nineteenth week. Senator Rufus Keel has not written this week. Mr. Pratt states that he 'noticed.'

columns.headline: Arcade tenants deposit the August rent tomorrow; clerk to hold 1,236 dollars
columns.body: Mr. Nathan Ewald states that the Vantry Arcade's tenants will deposit the August rent of 412 dollars with the Municipal Court clerk at 10 a.m. tomorrow, when he will hold 1,236 dollars for Signal Ground Rents Inc. The company's box is unopened since July 15.

columns.headline: July's heat: 16 days of 90 degrees or more, the most since 1921
columns.body: The temperature reached 90 degrees or more on 16 days in July, the most since July 1921, the Weather Bureau states, the highest being 97. Twenty-one persons died of the heat in the city, three of them in Queens. The Bureau forecasts a cooler August.

record.wire: LATE WIRE: WORS 1610 was not heard last night, the Radio Division states, at any of its three places.

speaker.ear: Fair. High 85. Wednesday. The Zeppelin goes up tomorrow. So does the rent.

lead.headline: The Zeppelin casts off tomorrow, and Lakehurst stands by to take the line
lead.deck: Dr. Eckener wires 'Weather good'; the Navy's seven stations ready to hear her coming from the third; three hundred and fifty sailors have caught the rope so often the rope is tired
lead.body: Tomorrow the Graf Zeppelin leaves Friedrichshafen for Lakehurst, and last night Dr. Eckener wired the Navy two words, 'Weather good,' which is one more than Dr. Strand usually manages. From Saturday the Navy's seven stations from Lakehurst to Montauk will listen for her engines. The three hundred and fifty sailors have caught the weighted rope every day for a fortnight and are now very good at it. Our office boy's application for a berth came back yesterday, with the sandwiches, uneaten.

columns.headline: July signs off at ninety, sixteen times over
columns.body: Sixteen days of ninety or more this July, the Weather Bureau says, the most since 1921. Three people in Queens died of it, and we are sorry. Nell the ice horse came through, and so did Duchess. August, the Bureau says, will be cooler. The Bureau said that about July.

columns.headline: The Arcade's August rent goes in tomorrow, and the clerk's drawer is overloaded
columns.body: Tomorrow at ten the Arcade's tenants take the August rent to the court clerk, who will then hold twelve hundred and thirty-six dollars for a company that never calls. Mr. Raab's papers are still in its box. The grey coat has not been back. The pool favours Friday.

columns.headline: The Senate's 'resent' goes nineteen weeks, and Keel stops calling
columns.body: Nineteen weeks in the Albany vault, and the one word on the Senate's March record is still unclaimed. This week Senator Keel did not write. The clerk, Mr. Pratt, says he noticed. We think Mr. Pratt misses him.

speaker.wire: LATE WIRE: Friedrichshafen, midnight their time: the Zeppelin out of her shed, nose to the wind, and the Navy at Lakehurst listening early.
